answers.answer: Shuffle the Factory deck, randomly select players + 1 cards face-down onto the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: “number of players + 1”; “11 marked territories”; “lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”

answers.answer: The character starts at the home base; two workers start one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining it; four mechs go over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in green Player Mat boxes marked with a black square; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on the bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token beside the Player Mat, ready for first placement. Leave faction one-time recruit spaces empty. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 enumerate mat assignments and all starting pieces.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action, either one, or both. If taking both, top must precede bottom. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains can pay a bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before the action; then choose as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefit as desired. Exact bottom-row resource costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “different section”; “full cost”; “as much or as little”; top-row gains may pay bottom-row cost.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls that territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities; you keep those abilities without control, except an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Pay action resource costs from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker controls its territory; “You keep those abilities even without control”; pay from “any territories you currently control.”

answers.answer: No. Normal Move allows up to two different units one adjacent territory each, and the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. Being carried does not count as a worker’s own movement, so a transported worker may subsequently move itself. All units (characters, mechs, workers) can carry any number of resources; only mechs may additionally carry any number of your workers, never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: “two different units”; “cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice”; “Being carried does not count”; only mechs carry workers.

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech entering a territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn. The workers immediately retreat to their home base, leave resources behind, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. It is not combat. Your workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers immediately retreat; lose “one popularity per worker, down to zero”; worker cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve any combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: “Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats before the bottom-row action”; “attacker chooses multiple-combat order.”

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card (before upgrades); a built Monument also gives one popularity. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards to form a new deck; if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity (before upgrades); a built Armory also gives one power. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker. If all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade sections state costs, choices, building bonuses, placement, and empty-deck handling.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers are taken from the Player Mat left to right after payment and placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs affect future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3: pay in full, choose up to two territories, and take workers after payment; “You may decline.”

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes. Both amounts vary by mat and upgrades. Upgrade moves a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy places a mech from the Faction Mat on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after all upgrades, mechs, structures, or recruits are completed, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy, and continued payment after completing pieces are stated explicitly.

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents’ structures. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill provides its bonus production territory only while you control it; an enemy unit can remove your control, so it then cannot produce. A Mine is your personal tunnel for your unit movement, including Factory Move, even when enemy-controlled; the ability remains yours despite lack of control. Opponents cannot use your structure abilities.
answers.evidence: Build: placement and permanence; Mill works “only while controlled”; Mine is personal and works “even when enemy-controlled.”

answers.answer: Put the recruited token permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus space on your Faction Mat and immediately gain two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards (your choice). The ongoing bonus is determined by the Player Mat circle uncovered where the recruit was removed: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. Resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits specify placement, four one-time benefits, action-based ongoing benefit, and resolution order.

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly and simultaneously chooses dial power from 0 to the smaller of seven and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even at zero dial power; Rusviet People’s Army adds one card if any workers are present. Combat abilities are used attacker first, then defender, if both have abilities. Reveal dials/cards simultaneously, add dial and card values, and attacker wins ties. Both players lose their dial power from their tracks and discard every played card face-up; card values do not reduce track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3 give simultaneous secret choices, card limits, ability order, payment, and attacker wins ties.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie provides its stated aggressor combat exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 4–5 state retreats, resources, popularity, combat stars and loser card reward.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token and draw a card before any following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay no additional normal action costs and receive no additional mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after Move and all combats; contested loss leaves token; gains go to encounter territory; no normal action costs or mat benefits.

answers.answer: Every player’s character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if needed), looks at the available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. A Factory card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, subject to the normal no-repeat rule except Rusviet. Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories in that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement and stop rules apply.
answers.evidence: Factory section states each player's first visit, permanent card, action and movement rules.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you may wait, but must meet all requirements at reveal. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed. Saxony keeps the other card after the first and may complete both starting objectives and score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: own turn timing, requirements at reveal, both cards discarded to bottom, Saxony exception.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony’s exception. Stars are permanent even if power or popularity later drops, and another player’s star never blocks your goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists achievements, permanence, no blocking, and immediate sixth-star end.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect the primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat. For neighbors’ power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step; after a sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star sequence spells out bottom-action collection, pending battle undo, and neighbor recruit order.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, the table’s 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources: 5 stars = $20; four ordinary territories plus Factory (five territories for scoring) = $15; 13 resources = six pairs = $12. These add $47 to held coins (the summary’s example says $53, but its displayed arithmetic is $20 + $21 + $12, treating territories as seven; that example conflicts with the stated prompt’s four ordinary plus Factory, which is five total territories). The selected structure bonus is also scored, even if enemies control your structures’ territories. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table gives 7–12 payouts; Factory counts as three territories total; structure bonus remains eligible; tiebreak order listed. Example says “$20 + $21 + $12 = $53.”

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into a home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea’s unlocked Wayfare. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: “A home base is not a territory”; default restrictions and inactive placeholders.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers. Lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table and resources section: workers are not resources; resource tokens have no supply limit.

answers.answer: All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; a mech can also carry any number of your workers mid-movement, but never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, so the extra step may be before or after it. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move section states resource carriage, mech worker carriage, Speed and tunnel-step rules.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: “Any unit may enter” enemy-structure-only territory; “All printed tunnel territories are adjacent” for any unit.

answers.answer: You never pay only part of a cost. If you cannot afford any action, take a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action. Since you last used Move, select a different section as usual; no partial Produce payment is legal.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Never pay only part of a cost”; unaffordable actions permit a dead turn by moving to a different section.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These trigger as part of those actions. You retain structure abilities even without control, so an enemy occupant does not take them away; the exception is that an uncontrolled Mill cannot produce.
answers.evidence: Bolster/Trade building bonuses; control section says abilities remain without control except Mill production.

answers.answer: Riverwalk lets the character and mechs enter the listed destinations: Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Nordic forests and mountains; Polania villages and mountains; Saxony forests and mountains. Nordic Swim applies to workers alone, lets them cross rivers to any land terrain but not lakes, and does not help character/mechs; it gives no lake movement to Nordic mechs.
answers.evidence: Faction ability table lists Riverwalk destinations; Nordic Swim description expressly excludes lakes and character/mechs.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels (including your Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use either shortcut.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township specify locations and character/mech movement.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or your Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery also applies before combat, but you may pay one power to reduce the opponent’s power by two; it is once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Disarm and Artillery ability descriptions specify timing, amount, and per-combat frequency.

answers.answer: With two mechs and three workers present, Rusviet may play three combat cards total (one extra card total if at least one worker is present, plus the two participating mechs). Workers alone never fight; a character or mech is required.
answers.evidence: People’s Army: “Two mechs and three workers allow three cards”; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from a territory or home base to your own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot move them to an active opponent’s home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare description specifies allowed and excluded home bases.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat and not per unit. Crimea Coercion lets you spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of that card’s value.
answers.evidence: Scout and Coercion descriptions state timing, amount, limit and card value rule.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and move from any lake to any other lake, but Polania has no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, workers on lakes need a mech to move off; carried workers or resources cannot be left behind on a lake when their carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Lake-capable faction rules distinguish Seaworthy and Submerge; explicitly require carried pieces to leave with carrier.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not prevent loss for driving out undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Camaraderie description gives combat-aggressor condition and excludes undefended-worker displacement.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first gain can pay the cost of the second. The summary does not state a special number of cards: encounter resolution draws one card. You must pay the printed cost for each selected option, and may take as little of each benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Meander: “up to two different options”; first gain can pay second cost; Encounter rules require printed cost and allow reduced benefit.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter-token territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. Resolve the encounter only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Move and Encounter rules say character stops; encounter follows whole Move action and all combats; Factory Move is covered.

answers.answer: Combat-card count is public but card contents are secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but a player need not reveal their total coin value. During combat players may conceal whether they have committed cards until reveal.
answers.evidence: Setup information paragraph specifies public count, secret contents/objectives, and coin total disclosure.

answers.answer: Informal agreements are unenforceable. Coins are the only tangible items exchangeable; in tournament play even coin exchanges for deals or alliances are forbidden. A payment cannot cancel combat already initiated by moving units onto opposing units; fight after Move, though bribes may influence the outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section specifies exchange limits, enforceability, and initiated combat.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory, $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3, and $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4, and $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Pool resources across controlled territories and ignore an odd leftover token.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and text directly state tiers, lake/base treatment, and complete resource pairs.

answers.answer: For each adjacency tile, count each unique qualifying feature once across all structures. Rivers do not break adjacency. Encounter locations count even after their token is removed. Tunnel-adjacency scoring counts unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines; lake-adjacency scoring counts unique lakes; encounter-adjacency scoring counts unique printed encounter locations. Payouts for tunnels: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9. Encounters: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9. Lakes: 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table gives uniqueness, river, removed-token, Mine, and all three payout schedules.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures in a row scores only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break the line: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Structures on farms/tundras counts qualifying structures on both terrain types combined: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus table lists criteria and payouts for tunnels, rows, and combined farms/tundras.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, even for workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake. Polania Camaraderie may provide the specified exception if its conditions are met.
answers.evidence: Combat step 5 explicitly includes workers carried by defeated mech on a lake.

answers.answer: No. A placed popularity star is permanent, but current popularity can later drop and determines final scoring. Another player’s star does not block the same goal, so two factions can each earn that achievement’s star.
answers.evidence: Stars section: star permanent despite later popularity drop; other players’ stars never block a goal.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order, clockwise: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts. Seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses are triggered by the active player’s immediate left and right neighbors, in active-player, left, right order.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2 and 5; Ongoing recruits gives adjacent-neighbor trigger/order.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter the lake from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Movement rules define rivers and lakes and state lake entry from any adjoining surrounding land territory.

answers.answer: No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: “Show the encounter card to all players”; show artwork and read capitalized thematic text; options need not all be read.

answers.answer: No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: “No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.”

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure states the next player may begin after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action.

answers.answer: A section’s top and bottom actions are each optional once on that turn; the same top or bottom action cannot be taken a second time that turn. If taking both, top precedes bottom. Rusviet’s exception allows repeating a section from the previous turn, including its Factory card; the summary does not describe a second same-turn action as available.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: take that section’s top action once, then bottom action once; Rusviet may repeat a section from last turn.

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: “Alternatively gain $1.”

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat, including after retreat; they retreat to their home base. Produce uses workers left to right from the Player Mat, after payment, and exposed costs affect only future Produce actions.
answers.evidence: Produce: “Workers never return to the Player Mat”; retreat sends workers to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and/or zero popularity.
answers.evidence: Combat: “You may attack with zero power/popularity.”

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; ordinary factions simply cannot earn more than two combat stars.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4: “You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.”

answers.answer: A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option; it cannot decline to choose any option or select an unaffordable coin/popularity option. It must pay the printed cost, but may take as little of its chosen benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: without Meander, “must choose one affordable option”; may take as little of benefit as desired.

answers.answer: No. Combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly, along with any cards. They reveal simultaneously after both choices are made.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: “simultaneously and secretly choose”; “Reveal simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: “Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.”

answers.answer: No. A star is placed as soon as its goal is achieved, so you cannot decline or delay a qualifying star to avoid ending the game. An objective is different: it must be revealed on your own turn, and you may wait to reveal it, provided you meet all requirements when you do.
answers.evidence: Stars section says place “as soon as” achieved; Objectives says “You may wait” to reveal a completed objective.

answers.answer: Normally no: units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Movement rules: “Units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes”; abilities provide exceptions.

answers.answer: No. The recruit is placed permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus space on the Faction Mat and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit is put permanently on a one-time bonus; “It cannot later move.”

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter. A character entering the token territory stops and the encounter is resolved after the Move action and combats if it remains there.
answers.evidence: Encounters: “Only a character triggers an encounter.”

answers.answer: A controlled Mill provides one bonus production territory in addition to the normal territories selected (so up to three total). The Mill itself counts as one producing worker; each actual worker there also produces normally, so their output is added rather than substituted. The Mill can produce without an actual worker present, using the terrain table.
answers.evidence: Produce: Mill gives one bonus territory; counts as a worker; actual workers produce too; can produce without an actual worker.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish or preserve control; leaving the last unit from a territory where you have no structure means you no longer control it.
answers.evidence: Control section defines control by unit or uncontested structure; resources are not listed as establishing control.

answers.answer: Build is paid with wood; Enlist is paid with food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row resources: “Upgrade oil; Deploy metal; Build wood; Enlist food.”
